Analyzing the image:

**Visual observations:**
- Large, irregular brown/grey necrotic area covering a substantial portion of the leaf
- The lesion has an uneven, somewhat papery texture
- Irregular edges between healthy green tissue and the affected area
- No distinct concentric rings or yellow halos visible
- No orange/yellow powdery deposits visible on the leaf surface

**Matching against classes:**

- **Brown_Eye_Spot / Berry_Blotch**: Both require small circular spots (up to 15mm) with concentric rings (grey center, dark brown ring, yellow margin) — not present here.
- **Rust**: Requires yellow/orange powdery lesions on the lower leaf surface — not visible.
- **Phoma**: Circular dark spots up to 2cm, infection starting at apical parts, leaves curve/crack — the lesion is much larger and more irregular than Phoma's described spots.
- **Cerscospora**: No symptom description provided; typically grey leaf spots — possible but no distinct pattern visible.
- **Miner**: Describes "large necrotic patches caused by larval mining" developing from mines under the leaf epidermis, with irregular brown spots on the upper surface — the large, irregular necrotic patch seen here fits this description best.

The large, irregular, coalesced brown/grey necrotic area on the upper leaf surface is most consistent with advanced leaf miner damage where mining larvae have caused extensive tissue death.
